extracted.intended_audience: users of the GAP computer algebra system; mathematicians and programmers using GAP for combinatorics and number theory computations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP functions and definitions related to combinatorics (combinations, partitions, tuples, permutations, Stirling/Bell numbers, derangements) and number types (rationals, cyclotomics, Fibonacci/Lucas, permanents). Describes semantics, representations, counts, ordering, and implementation notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stirling numbers of the second kind - definition and recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Stirling numbers of the second kind S2(n,k) are defined by S2(0,0)=1, S2(n,0)=S2(0,k)=0 if n,k ≠ 0, and the recurrence S2(n,k)=k*S2(n-1,k)+S2(n-1,k-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinatorial interpretation: S2(n,k) is the number of ways to partition a set of n elements into k pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets. They appear as coefficients in expansions and relate to Stirling numbers of the first kind, Bell numbers, and binomial coefficients. Also S2(n,k)=S1(-k,-n) if n,k<0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinations(mset[, k]) - semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinations(mset[, k]) returns the set of all combinations of the multiset mset with k elements; if k omitted returns all combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A combination is an unordered selection without repetitions, represented by a sorted sublist of mset. For a proper set mset there are binomial(|mset|, k) combinations. When k is omitted the set of all combinations equals the power set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory-efficient iteration for combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use IteratorOfCombinations or EnumeratorOfCombinations to loop over combinations without building the full list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IteratorOfCombinations returns an Iterator that produces combinations one by one (may save memory). EnumeratorOfCombinations returns an Enumerator (currently without k argument variant). Ordering between these and Combinations() may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorOfCombinations / EnumeratorOfCombinations behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorOfCombinations(mset[,k]) returns an Iterator for combinations; EnumeratorOfCombinations(mset) returns an Enumerator of combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If k provided only combinations of size k are produced. Enumerator currently implemented only without k. Ordering of produced combinations can differ from Combinations() and from each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrCombinations - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrCombinations(mset[, k]) returns the number of combinations Combinations(mset,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compute counts (e.g., poker hands example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangements(mset[, k]) - semantics and count
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangements(mset[, k]) returns the set of arrangements (ordered selections without repetitions) of multiset mset containing k elements; if k omitted returns all arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An arrangement is an ordered selection represented by a list possibly in different order. For proper set mset there are |mset|!/(|mset|-k)! arrangements with k elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrArrangements - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrArrangements(mset[, k]) returns the number of Arrangements(mset,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain counts without materializing lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnorderedTuples(set,k) - semantics and count
rubrics_metrics.description: UnorderedTuples(set, k) returns the set of all unordered tuples (unordered selections with repetitions) of length k from set, represented by a sorted list of length k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are binomial(|set|+k-1, k) such tuples. The returned set implies the last index runs fastest: ordering places tuples with smaller elements earlier. Useful for poker-like dice examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrUnorderedTuples - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrUnorderedTuples(set, k) returns the number of UnorderedTuples(set,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute counts such as number of dice hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuples(set,k) - semantics and count
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuples(set, k) returns the set of all ordered tuples (ordered selections with repetitions) of length k of set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ordered tuple is represented by a list of length k; there are |set|^k such tuples. The last index runs fastest (lexicographic variant), and Tuples can be seen as the k-fold Cartesian product.

rubrics_metrics.name: EnumeratorOfTuples / IteratorOfTuples - behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: EnumeratorOfTuples(set,k) and IteratorOfTuples(set,k) provide enumerator/iterator views of Tuples(set,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These avoid storing all tuples physically; IteratorOfTuples returns tuples in lexicographic order; EnumeratorOfTuples creates entries on demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrTuples - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrTuples(set,k) returns the number of Tuples(set,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain cardinalities without enumeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermutationsList(mset) - semantics and count
rubrics_metrics.description: PermutationsList(mset) returns the set of permutations of the multiset mset; a permutation is a list containing the same elements possibly in different order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mset is a proper set there are |mset|! permutations; with multiplicities k1,k2,... the number is |mset|!/(k1!k2!...), the multinomial coefficient. Arrangements generalizes PermutationsList by allowing specified size.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrPermutationsList - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrPermutationsList(mset) returns the number of permutations returned by PermutationsList(mset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to gauge the size before enumerating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derangements(list) - semantics and formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Derangements(list) returns the set of all derangements (fixpoint-free permutations) of list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the list has all distinct elements, the number of derangements is |list|!*(1/2! - 1/3! + 1/4! - ... + (-1)^n/n!). Relation: NrPermutationsList([1..n])/NrDerangements([1..n]) approximates e; derangements model problems like sending letters to people with no one receiving their own letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrDerangements - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrDerangements(list) returns the number of derangements of list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compute counts (examples given for small n).

rubrics_metrics.name: PartitionsSet(set[, k]) - semantics and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: PartitionsSet(set[, k]) returns the set of all unordered partitions of the set into k pairwise disjoint nonempty sets; if k omitted returns all partitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unordered partition is represented by a sorted list of such sets. There are Bell(|set|) partitions in total and S2(|set|,k) partitions with k blocks. Note: PartitionsSet does not currently support multisets and there is no ordered counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrPartitionsSet - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrPartitionsSet(set[, k]) returns the number of PartitionsSet(set,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for precomputing cardinalities (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitions(n[, k]) - integer partitions semantics and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Partitions(n[, k]) returns the set of all (unordered) partitions of the positive integer n into sums with k summands; if k omitted returns all partitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unordered integer partition is represented as a list [p1,...,pk] in nonincreasing order (p1≥p2≥...≥pk). There are approximately exp(pi*sqrt(2n/3))/(4n*sqrt(3)) partitions asymptotically; use NrPartitions for exact counts. Partitions correspond to conjugacy classes of the symmetric group, so p(n)=NrPartitions(n). For larger n use IteratorOfPartitions for memory efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorOfPartitions - behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorOfPartitions(n) returns an iterator of partitions of n in lexicographic order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to iterate without building the full list when n is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorOfPartitionsSet - options
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorOfPartitionsSet(set[, k[, flag]]) returns an iterator for unordered partitions of set into nonempty disjoint sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If k given and flag omitted or false, only partitions of size k are computed. If flag is true and k given, only partitions of size at most k are computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrPartitions - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrPartitions(n[, k]) returns the number of Partitions(n,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example counts are provided; use to obtain exact values such as NrPartitions(100).

rubrics_metrics.name: OrderedPartitions(n[, k]) - semantics, counts, and warning
rubrics_metrics.description: OrderedPartitions(n[, k]) returns the set of all ordered partitions (compositions) of n into k summands; if k omitted returns all ordered partitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ordered partition is represented by [p1,...,pk]; total number is 2^{n-1}, and there are binomial(n-1,k-1) with k summands. Warning: Do not call OrderedPartitions with n much larger than 15 because the list will become too large (memory/time explosion).

rubrics_metrics.name: NrOrderedPartitions - count
rubrics_metrics.description: NrOrderedPartitions(n[, k]) returns the number of OrderedPartitions(n,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show rapid growth (e.g., NrOrderedPartitions(20)=524288).

rubrics_metrics.name: PartitionsGreatestLE / PartitionsGreatestEQ - restricted-part functions
rubrics_metrics.description: PartitionsGreatestLE(n,m) returns unordered partitions of n with parts ≤ m; PartitionsGreatestEQ(n,m) returns those with greatest part equal to m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to restrict partitions by part size or greatest part.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedPartitions(n, set[, k]) - restricted-part partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictedPartitions(n, set[, k]) returns restricted partitions of n where summands must be elements of set; if k omitted returns all restricted partitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation is as for Partitions (nonincreasing lists). Use NrRestrictedPartitions to count. Example: coin-change problems can be modeled with this function.

rubrics_metrics.name: SignPartition(pi) - permutation sign from cycle structure
rubrics_metrics.description: SignPartition(pi) returns the sign (±1) of a permutation with cycle structure pi; sign 1 are even partitions, sign -1 odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This maps partitions to parity and identifies kernel of sign homomorphism (alternating group).

rubrics_metrics.name: AssociatedPartition(pi) - transpose of Young diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: AssociatedPartition(pi) returns the partition obtained by transposing the Young diagram of pi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for conjugation and Young diagram manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerPartition(pi,k) - cycle-structure power map
rubrics_metrics.description: PowerPartition(pi,k) returns the partition corresponding to the k-th power of a permutation with cycle structure pi: each part l of pi is replaced by d=gcd(l,k) parts l/d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes power map on symmetric groups; result is a partition of the same n.

rubrics_metrics.name: PartitionTuples(n,r) / NrPartitionTuples - r-tuples of partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: PartitionTuples(n,r) returns the list of all r-tuples of partitions which together form a partition of n; NrPartitionTuples returns the number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: r-tuples of partitions are used to describe classes/characters of wreath products with symmetric groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: BetaSet(alpha) - beta-set of a partition
rubrics_metrics.description: BetaSet(alpha) for partition alpha returns the list obtained by reversing alpha and adding [0,1,2,...] of same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in representation theory; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibonacci(n) - definition and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Fibonacci(n) returns the nth Fibonacci number with F1=F2=1 and recurrence F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n; for negative n define F_n = (-1)^{n+1} F_{-n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closed form via φ (golden ratio) noted; gcd(F_m,F_n)=F_{gcd(m,n)}. Fibonacci(k) is a special case of Lucas sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucas(P,Q,k) - Lucas sequences definition and relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Lucas(P,Q,k) returns the kth values of Lucas sequences with parameters P,Q as a list [U_k, V_k, Q^k]; U_0=0,U_1=1 with recurrence U_k = P U_{k-1} - Q U_{k-2}, similar for V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined via roots α,β of x^2 - P x + Q: U_k=(α^k-β^k)/(α-β), V_k = α^k+β^k. Many doubling and parity relations given; Fibonacci is Lucas(1,-1,k)[1].

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent(mat) - definition and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent(mat) returns the permanent of matrix mat: sum over permutations of product of entries, same as determinant but without permutation sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent is not multilinear or alternating but has important combinatorial properties. Examples show its combinatorial counts (e.g., projective plane permutations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational representation - canonical form
rubrics_metrics.description: Rational numbers are represented as a reduced pair (numerator, denominator) of integers with gcd=1; numerator carries the sign and denominator is always positive. If denominator is 1 the rational is represented as an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because integer arithmetic supports arbitrary-size integers, rational arithmetic is exact even for very large numerators/denominators. Examples illustrate normalization and sign rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationals global and IsRationals filter
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationals is the field Q of rationals represented as cyclotomic numbers; IsRationals(obj) returns true for a prime field consisting of cyclotomic numbers (e.g., the GAP object Rationals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size(Rationals) may be infinity; IsRationals helps detect rational domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRat / IsPosRat / IsNegRat categories
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRat is the category every rational number lies in (subcategory of IsCyc). IsPosRat and IsNegRat classify positive and negative rationals respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test object categories in GAP; IsRat(true) returns false as it is a function, not a rational.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumeratorRat and DenominatorRat - accessors and invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: NumeratorRat(rat) returns the numerator (which carries the sign); DenominatorRat(rat) returns the positive denominator. For integers NumeratorRat is identity and DenominatorRat returns 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerator/denominator are made relatively prime by construction; examples show normalization behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rat(elm) - parsing to rationals
rubrics_metrics.description: Rat(elm) returns a rational corresponding to elm: if elm is a numeric string with digits, optional leading '-', '/', and '.', it is parsed into a rational; if elm is already rational returns it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: String() can produce string representation; examples show Rat("1/2"), Rat("3.14159") producing rationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random(Rationals) - pseudorandom rationals
rubrics_metrics.description: Random(Rationals) returns pseudo random rationals which are quotient of two random integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Random documentation for integer generation details; useful for randomized experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic basics - E(n) and Cyclotomics domain
rubrics_metrics.description: E(n) returns primitive nth root of unity exp(2πi/n). Cyclotomics is the domain of all cyclotomic numbers (sums of roots of unity with rational coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclotomics are entered and printed as sums of roots of unity; E(n)^k, combinations, and operations behave as field arithmetic. Example shows E(9), E(6), E(12) usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCyclotomic / IsCyc categories and family membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects in CyclotomicsFamily lie in category IsCyclotomic; most except infinity and unknowns also lie in IsCyc. IsCyclotomic/IsCyc detect membership; infinity lies in IsInfinity instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish cyclotomic numbers, infinity, and unknowns. Examples illustrate IsCyclotomic/in IsCyc checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIntegralCyclotomic - cyclotomic integers
rubrics_metrics.description: A cyclotomic is integral (cyclotomic integer) if coefficients of its minimal polynomial over Q are integers; equivalently external representation is a list of integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roots of unity and many algebraic integers are integral; rationals non-integers are not. Use IsIntegralCyclotomic to test; Int can find nearby cyclotomic integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Int and RoundCyc - nearby integral cyclotomic and rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Int(cyc) finds a cyclotomic integer near cyc by applying integer rounding to external-representation coefficients. RoundCyc(cyc) rounds coefficients in the Zumbroich basis to nearest integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to coerce/approximate cyclotomics to integral cyclotomics; examples show behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: String, Conductor, CoeffsCyc, ExtRepOfObj - cyclotomic utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: String(cyc) gives printable string; Conductor(cyc) returns smallest n such that cyc is in nth cyclotomic field; CoeffsCyc(cyc,N) returns coefficient vector relative to N-th Zumbroich basis if N multiple of conductor; ExtRepOfObj(cyc) returns external representation (coeffs at conductor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficients allow reconstruction cyc = CoeffsCyc(cyc,N) * List(1..N, j-> E(N)^(j-1)). CoeffsCyc fails if N not a multiple of conductor. Examples show typical calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: DenominatorCyc - denominator for cyclotomics
rubrics_metrics.description: DenominatorCyc(cyc) returns the smallest positive integer n such that n*cyc is a cyclotomic integer; for rationals equals DenominatorRat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to detect denominators needed to clear denominators in cyclotomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: DescriptionOfRootOfUnity(root) - identify root of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: DescriptionOfRootOfUnity(root) returns [n,e] of coprime positive integers such that root = E(n)^e, for known roots of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not checked whether input is root of unity; useful to canonicalize roots of unity. Example: E(9) -> [9,1], -E(3) -> [6,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGaussInt / IsGaussRat - Gaussian integer/rational tests
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGaussInt(x) returns true if x is a Gaussian integer (a+b*E(4) with integers a,b). IsGaussRat(x) returns true if x is a Gaussian rational (a+b*E(4) with rationals a,b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detects membership in Gaussian integer/rational subrings.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultField for cyclotomics
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultField(list) returns the smallest cyclotomic field containing the given elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field(...) returns the smallest field (not necessarily cyclotomic) containing elements; DefaultField ensures cyclotomic field selection (vector space over Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity and -infinity objects and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: infinity and -infinity are special GAP objects in CyclotomicsFamily used as top/bottom elements; they lie in IsInfinity and not in IsCyc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as return values for operations like Size on infinite domains; some arithmetic operations defined (infinity+infinity=infinity). Distinguish via IsInfinity / IsCyc tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering/comparisons of cyclotomics
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison operators <,<=,=,>=,>,<> are defined on cyclotomics: rationals ordered naturally, rationals < irrational cyclotomics, infinity largest. For two irrationals different conductors: smaller conductor considered smaller; same conductor compared via external representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this ordering for sorting and comparisons; examples illustrate comparisons between E(5), E(6), rationals, and infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATLAS irrationalities utilities (EB..EH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions EB(N), EC(N), ED(N), EE(N), EF(N), EG(N), EH(N) provide predefined ATLAS irrationalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are helpers for special irrationalities used in ATLAS of finite groups; further reference provided in subsequent sections.
